issue_context.title: BUG: `pd.infer_freq` incompatible with `Series["timestamp[s][pyarrow]"]`.
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd

data = ["2022-01-01T10:00:00", "2022-01-01T10:00:30", "2022-01-01T10:01:00"]
pd_series = pd.Series(data).astype("timestamp[s][pyarrow]")
pd_index = pd.Index(data).astype("timestamp[s][pyarrow]")
assert pd.infer_freq(pd_index.values) == "30s"  # ✅
assert pd.infer_freq(pd_series.values) == "30s"  # ✅
assert pd.infer_freq(pd_index) == "30s"  # ✅
assert pd.infer_freq(pd_series) == "30s"  # ❌
```


### Issue Description

```
TypeError: cannot infer freq from a non-convertible dtype on a Series of timestamp[s][pyarrow]
```

However, it works with `Index`-objects of this dtype, or if we call `.values` (which converts it to `list[pd.Timedelta]`)

### Expected Behavior

There should be no `TypeError` here, especially since it works with Index objects of this dtype.

review_comments: I am a bit surprised by this comment, isn't `pandas.api.types.is_` supposed to be a single source of truth of what is considered a certain data type? How do you remember what are all the conditions to check otherwise?
For internal usages, checking `dtype.kind` is more performant than `api.types` functions so that is preferred
Ah I guess I accidentally removed checking for timedelta. Although no tests failed. I am adding some tests for timedeltas as well.

There is another bug: when trying with `Index["duration[s][pyarrow]"]`, it complains about the property `asi8` missing. asi8 is [denoted as deprecated on general index types](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/8dab54d6573f7186ff0c3b6364d5e4dd635ff3e7/pandas/core/indexes/base.py#L674-L689). Moreover, the `FrequencyInferer` assumes numpy dtype and makes use of internals (like `index._data._ndarray`)

the easiest workaround would be to cast to numpy, but I guess we want to avoid that and keep dtype as pyarrow inside the ops.
